core_obligations: Parts (1) and (2) (proof lines 391-400): part (1) follows from the theorem that a birational morphism of Noetherian spaces is an isomorphism over a dense open, and part (2) follows from part (3) together with the lemma reducing the codimension one case to the finite case, since finite morphisms have finite fibres.

Reduce to a finite morphism (proof lines 400-408): for a point x as in (3), the proper morphism with finite fibre over x is finite in a neighbourhood of x by the cited lemma, so one may assume f is finite.

Etale localization (proof lines 408-418): choose an affine scheme X' etale over X and a point x' mapping to x; it suffices to find an open neighbourhood of x' over which the base change is an isomorphism, because then the image of that neighbourhood is an open neighbourhood of x in X by descent of the property along the etale cover; the base change is again finite and birational, and since a finite morphism is affine one reduces to the case of a finite birational morphism of Noetherian affine schemes with a normal local ring at the point, which is the cited scheme case.
proof_roadmap: Read parts (1) and (2) off from the known dense open isomorphism and the reduction to finite morphisms.
Make the morphism finite in a neighbourhood of the point using the finite fibre hypothesis.
Etale localize to affine schemes and invoke the case of schemes.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a birational proper morphism with reduced source onto a Noetherian algebraic space, the maximal open over which the morphism is an isomorphism contains every point of codimension zero, every codimension one point with normal local ring, and every point with finite fibre and normal local ring (statement lines 373-389). The proof (proof lines 391-416) uses the dense open isomorphism for part (1), reduces part (2) to part (3), makes the morphism finite near the point using the finite fibre hypothesis, and etale localizes to affine schemes to invoke the case of schemes. H2: three parts with four inputs, written out in full.
